/-!
# Erdős Problem 689
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)
* [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
-/

namespace Erdos689

/--
Let `n` be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class `a_p` for all primes
`2 ≤ p ≤ n` such that every integer in `[1,n]` satisfies at least two of the congruences
`≡ a_p (mod p)`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_689 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n,
      2 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 n |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card := by
  sorry

end Erdos689

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement chooses unrestricted natural representatives through a total function `a : ℕ → ℕ` and expresses double coverage by a filtered finset’s cardinality, rather than choosing residue classes on the bounded prime index set and explicitly requiring two distinct prime moduli.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Only values at primes p ≤ n are used. Every such prime is at least 2, and replacing a p by a p % p gives a canonical representative below p without changing any congruence. Conversely, canonical representatives can be extended arbitrarily to a total natural-valued function. Cardinality at least 2 is equivalent to the existence of two distinct primes satisfying the congruences. The prime predicate excludes 1 despite the filter interval starting at 1. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, `formal_question_iff_source` proves that the exact right-hand side is equivalent to an explicit threshold formulation with normalized representatives and two distinct primes; the proof does not depend on sorry axioms.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the cited Erdős page’s closed-interval, two-fold covering question. Green’s headline variant requires ten coverings, but its comments explicitly discuss replacing ten by two. The source still records OPEN; Bloom’s pinned comment says the proposed solutions await expert verification or publication, so no status update is warranted. Boundary checks confirmed that n = 0 is vacuous, n = 1 and 2 cannot work, and all 210 canonical residue choices for n = 7 fail; these small exceptions do not affect eventuality on ℕ. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings. The reviewed file remains identical to the specified commit.
